title: Profile of the rebuild path
evidence: Every edit redid work for the whole map; moving data cost about as much as computing it. One-node edit: 71–84 ms at 5k, 290–340 ms at 20k, 0.9–1.8 s at 50k.

title: Profile of the frame path and GPU
evidence: Panning cheap except whole-map view at 50k (2.4–4.4 ms script). GPU cost dominated by blended overdraw and 4x multisampling. WebKit ~40x slower per label raster.

title: Rust/WebAssembly and workers, measured in isolation
evidence: Flat tessellation kernel 2x faster in wasm (50k: 91→33 ms Chrome, 67→32 ms WebKit), bit-identical; copy-out costs 12–40 ms. Layout: typed-array TypeScript gets most of the wasm gain. JS worker pool slower in WebKit; wasm pool 2.5x at 8 workers. SharedArrayBuffer not practical in Tauri on macOS.

title: Native rendering spike: GPUI and wgpu
evidence: GPUI 0.2.2 cannot draw the 50k map (no custom shaders or retained buffers; 36 ms/frame at 5k). wgpu matches WebGL once WebGL stops re-uploading indices each frame. Screen was locked, so real 120 Hz presentation was not measured.

title: Draw visible branch runs from the resident index buffer; skip culling when the whole map is in view
evidence: Script per frame, 50k whole map: clean 3.47→0.94 ms, rope 4.10→0.92 (Chrome); 1.92→0.75 (WebKit).

title: Blending off for fully opaque branch meshes
evidence: GPU per frame at 50k zoom 1 (Chrome): clean 3.51→1.24 ms, rope 3.44→1.98. Within noise on the overall score.

title: Rect and shadow instances stay on the GPU at whole-map view
evidence: Script per frame at whole map: 50k soft-clay 1.96→1.44 (Chrome), 2.14→1.35 (WebKit). GPU buffers +6% for soft-clay.

title: No multisampling while the camera moves; full 4x frame 120 ms after it stops
evidence: Probe (Chrome GPU, moving frames, 50k): soft-clay whole map 6.16→2.17 ms, rope zoom 1 2.20→1.07. Resting frames bit-identical in both engines. Edges stair-step while moving.

title: Coarse index buffer for the branch mesh below zoom 0.02
evidence: Probe (Chrome GPU, 50k whole map): clean ~1.1→~0.45 ms; triangles 3.0M→0.57M. 0.005–0.05% of pixels change at that zoom.

title: Quarter-resolution shadow layer while the camera moves
evidence: At most 0.1–0.25 ms GPU, rounds overlap; visibly softer shadows. Reverted in 74f9878.

title: Text-layout cache sized to the map
evidence: Screening: rebuild at 50k clean 1123→995 ms (Chrome), 1338→1068 (WebKit). The official run for this commit is not usable (taken while the machine was busiest; rounds disagree).

title: Cheap per-node size lookup
evidence: Measured ceiling 20–25 ms of an ~800 ms edit at 50k; below the noise floor.

title: Rasterise a frame’s labels on one staging strip and upload as a batch
evidence: WebKit script per frame, 50k zoom 0.35: clean 1.43→0.82 ms. Text in a newly reached view fills in within 6 frames instead of 52 (WebKit). Byte-identical glyphs.

title: Skip the label loop when no label is large enough to draw; truthful pending-label count
evidence: Whole-map frames: 0.25–0.38 ms saved per frame at 50k in both engines.

title: While zooming, draw a label raster one size step off instead of re-rasterising
evidence: Probe (20k): Chrome zoom-sweep p95 3.5→1.8 ms; WebKit mean −24%. Labels are slightly soft or thin during a zoom gesture, exact one frame after it stops.

title: Stop cloning the CPU branch mesh to the main thread
evidence: Chrome heap −33% at 5k, −37% at 50k. Latency within noise.

title: Layout result as typed boxes plus JSON record lists
evidence: Screening score 0.966 / 0.948; edit at 50k 0.91 / 0.82. JSON was 2–6x cheaper than structured clone.

title: Document replica in the worker; edits sent as ops
evidence: Screening score 0.929 / 0.928; edit at 5k 0.83 / 0.72. One message per edit instead of 218.

title: Autosave and journal serialisation after the next frame
evidence: Screening score 0.957 / 0.951. Journal-path probe: add at 50k 629→583 ms (Chrome), 531→475 (WebKit).

title: Result in one message instead of pulled chunks
evidence: Latency within noise; longest main-thread task at 50k 75→84 ms. Reverted in 0b03056.

title: Decode branch specs on the main thread only when read
evidence: Main-thread result handling at 50k: 74–93→37–49 ms (Chrome), 50–69→32–34 ms (WebKit).

title: Decode adopted placements only when read
evidence: No gain; Chrome longest task 76→99 ms. Reverted in 4825198.

title: Flat vertex packing: one 32-bit colour write per run
evidence: Packer alone at 50k: 27→17.5 ms (Chrome), 21–23→13.4–14.6 ms (WebKit). Byte-identical.

title: Copy reused branch meshes in runs
evidence: Worker mesh step per edit at 50k: 35–47→24–32 ms (Chrome), 58–66→28–39 ms (WebKit).

title: Rust→WebAssembly flat tessellation and packing inside the layout worker
evidence: In-app, 50k theme switch: 999→964 ms (Chrome), 1089→1081 ms (WebKit). Holds 217 MB of wasm memory that is never released. Bit-identical output. Reverted in 17a8fb1.

title: Worker pool for tessellation
evidence: Best case about 25 ms of a 1,000–1,500 ms rebuild; JS-only variant loses in WebKit (sending specs costs 78–113 ms).

title: Typed-array tidy-tree layout kernel (plain TypeScript)
evidence: Warm layout 1.25x faster in both engines; Chrome first 50k call 71→34 ms. Bit-identical in 48 cases.

title: GPU-expanded branches: one record per branch, ribbon built in the vertex shader (flat tapered, rounded, line)
evidence: Screening: rebuild at 50k 0.90 / 0.82, edit 0.93 / 0.73; WebGL buffers at 50k 98→1.6 MB plus a 6.4 MB record texture; heap 167→75 MB. Whole-map GPU +0.35 ms.

title: Each GPU branch as one continuous strip
evidence: Whole-map GPU at 50k (Chrome): 2.17→1.22 ms (CPU-mesh parent: 1.07). Pixels identical to G1.

title: Organic and angular branch styles on the GPU
evidence: Chrome probe: worker mesh −62 to −72%; edit at 20k 298→231 ms. GPU +11 to +35% at whole map.

title: Soft clay and Rope materials on the GPU
evidence: Rope, Chrome, 2 rounds: load at 50k 1,498→943 ms; worker mesh 617→71 ms; buffers 189→2.2 MB plus 12.2 MB texture. Whole-map GPU +0.3 to +1.0 ms.

title: Profile of the four dimensional materials
evidence: Their rebuild cost is cold compiled code (a theme switch builds the mesh exactly once), not arithmetic or garbage collection.

title: Dimensional meshes built through small functions over one output object
evidence: Cold build at 50k in WebKit: rope 534–569→156–163 ms, lifted-arcs 194–198→84–92, paper-quilling 152–157→72–76. Bit-identical.

title: Narrower dimensional vertex format
evidence: No pixel-identical gain left; packing is bound by allocation, not the loop.

title: Reuse the shadow layer on resting frames
evidence: No gain; slower in 7 of 8 cases. Reverted in 272ad6a.

title: Far-zoom level of detail for dimensional meshes
evidence: The coarse index buffer already applies to every material.

title: Incremental node sizes
evidence: computeSizes per edit at 50k: 23–26→9–13 ms. Found and fixed a pre-existing bug (the worker replica kept a removed document field).

title: Incremental layout bookkeeping: untouched main branches keep their boxes and placements
evidence: settleLayout at 50k: 79–89→40–48 ms (Chrome), 59–64→35–37 ms (WebKit). Screening edit at 50k −9% / −20%.

title: Incremental branch specs
evidence: Screening: interaction −11% in both engines; edit at 5k −20%. Worker relayout at 50k −25 to −33%.

title: Incremental scene; skip empty badge and sketch scans
evidence: Screening: fold at 50k −12% / −14%. Worker compute for a one-node edit at 50k: ~260–300→~110–160 ms across IN1–IN4.

title: Cache each record’s JSON when packing the result
evidence: Edits at 50k −7 to −23%, but Chrome loads and theme switches +3 to +11% and +90 MB in the worker. Reverted in 64f2d3c.

title: Persistent, patchable branch-mesh buffers
evidence: Edit probe: Chrome −7 to −24% (50k clean 523→452 ms), WebKit −4 to −14%. Pixel-identical. Conflicts with the GPU-expanded design, which was chosen.

title: Ship the mesh ahead of its result and upload in slices
evidence: Dev probe: the frame showing a 50k theme switch draws in 14–20 ms instead of 61–66 ms.

title: Decode large results in 8 ms slices
evidence: No visible change; the longest task is the autosave after the frame (85–120 ms at 50k). Reverted in 48b4e01.

title: Packed vertices kept only on the GPU
evidence: Dev heap after loading 50k: clean 187→119 MB, rope 274→132 MB.
